newsitem.title: USA: Palmer Wireless shares off on deal concern.
newsitem.headline: Palmer Wireless shares off on deal concern.

text.p: Palmer Wireless Inc's shares fell as an analyst cut his rating on the stock amid growing concerns the regional wireless phone company is not going to find a buyer in the near future.
Furman Selz analyst Frederick Moran said he removed the stock from his brokerage's recommended list and cut it to neutral. He said he made no changes to earnings estimates.

"At this point we believe the company is totally subject to speculation as to whether the deal will be done to sell the company," Moran said in an interview, adding that, "We think the number of potential buyers has dwindled dramatically."
Palmer Wireless shares were off 3/8 point at 10-3/4 in late-afternoon trading Thursday.

The stock has come full circle in recent months, after rising above 15 in late February as rumors emerged that Palmer's main owners were seeking bidders for the company. It fell back this week as suitors failed to materialize.

Palmer owns a contiguous set of wireless phone properties stretching from South Carolina to Florida, making it an attractive target for national wireless companies seeking to fill in gaps in their national networks, analysts said.

Smith Barney Thomas Lee said in comments published in late March that he believed the company has been for sale since early February. Other analysts said the company has hired Goldman Sachs as its banker to handle negotiations.
Reached late last week, M. Wayne Wisehart, the chief financial officer at Palmer Wireless, declined to comment on what he called "rumors in the marketplace" that Palmer was in talks to be acquired.
He was not immediately available to comment Thursday.
The vast majority of Palmer Wireless stock is controlled by Palmer Communications Inc, a broadcasting company that has disposed of radio and TV properties in prior years.
One such player, 360 Communications Co, was an early Palmer bidder but has since withdrawn, according to Sharon Armburst, an analyst with Paul Kagan Associates.

Among other possible buyers considered possible by Wall Street analysts were AT&T Corp's Wireless unit, Bell Atlantic NYNEX Mobile, a unit of Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp, and SBC Communications Inc.
At least one analyst, who asked not to be named, dangled the possibility that an unnamed non-traditional communications provider could emerge as the sucessful bidder.
